svg.text: long dunes with a steep lee, red mesas, cacti and scrub; sun-bleached
A. At fight distance, noon: the ground profile, the cover silhouettes, the far land as a value ladder. The two grey figures are 75 units tall (a fighter): scale only, no character art.
Palette at noon (the world-light tint per sky key multiplies it; lit, mid and shade are the three faces of one surface; the far ladder is each ridge hazed toward the horizon)

Readability (docs/art/dynamic-sky.md section 6): worst aura against any tone 26.2 CIEDE2000 (rule: 20 or more), worst Protagonist or rival body against ground, rock or vegetation 15.6 (rule: 15 or more), over every sky key with the world-light tint.
B. What the fight leaves: scorched (a beam along the ground), cratered (an impact), burned (fire on what grows)
a glass trench: the sand fused into a dark green-black glassy band with a
bright pale edge (the prototype's GLASS TRENCH)
a deep clean bowl with a sharp rim; the dune lee collapses into it, the
fused glass patches and black-scorched rock; cacti blackened and split;
the dunes streaked grey with ash
C. Destruction in desert: the impact at three moments (burst, peak, settle). A sand plume: tall, wide, pale gold with a darker core; it falls fast and the dune face slumps and slides for a second.
D. Where it meets its neighbours (hard steps in colour, never a fade; the cover mixes over about a third of the width)
The dune sea runs to the shore; only the sand colour steps from pale to gold; no
Grass breaks into tufts on bare sand; scrub, then dunes; the ground steps from
green to gold in five hard bands.
Thorn scrub thins; red earth takes over from gold grass; acacias become single
Badlands: red mesas and scree fans spill from the grey rock; no soil between.
A black lava plain with sand drifted in streaks; basalt columns; the sand steps
Dry moor: the sand turns to bare weathered rock and thin heather; tors stand on
